P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, since 2 August 2019. Barbadians can open foreign-currency accounts at authorised dealers (commercial banks and some finance companies) without restriction, and the old rule requiring 70% of the funds to be surrendered was removed. Condition: you must use your foreign-currency balance for payments abroad before buying foreign exchange on the local market, and you must declare to the dealer that you have no other foreign currency available (Central Bank of Barbados, 2019).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 17.5%. Registration is required once taxable supplies reach BBD 200,000 a year; voluntary registration is allowed below that. The threshold rises to BBD 350,000 from 1 October 2026 (PwC: 'will be increased'; Kintsugi: proposed in the 2026 budget). Non-resident suppliers of digital services register and charge 17.5%.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (4) Local official channel: Open a foreign-currency account at a commercial bank (unrestricted since August 2019) and keep your USD earnings there. Spend that balance before buying foreign exchange locally (Central Bank of Barbados) (P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
